prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Company news: software, SaaS, database and cybersecurity.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed software, SaaS, database and cybersecurity companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.

## Cybersecurity — Analyst Actions [Software & SaaS]
- **CRWD** — Citi raised its price target to **$295 from $260** and maintained a **Buy** rating; shares fell **3.16%** on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[1]
- **PANW** — Citi raised its price target to **$440 from $410** and maintained a **Buy** rating; shares fell **2.76%** on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[1]
- **ZS** — Citi raised its price target to **$260 from $245** and maintained a **Buy** rating; shares fell **1.50%** on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[1]
- **OKTA** — Citi raised its price target to **$215 from $205** and maintained a **Neutral** rating; shares fell **3.33%** on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[1]
- **FTNT** — Wells Fargo analyst Richard Poland raised the price target to **$160 from $135** and maintained an **Underweight** rating; shares fell **2.91%** on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[1]

## **NOW** [Software & SaaS]
- **ServiceNow** President, Chief Product Officer and Chief Operating Officer Amit Zavery denied reports that the company intended to acquire AI customer-service startup Decagon; shares were reported up **5% to $146.93** during October 15 trading. (Yahoo Finance, October 15, source publication time not provided)[10]

## **CRM** [Software & SaaS]
- **Salesforce** shares were reported up **4% to $245.39** on October 15 in the same market reaction following ServiceNow’s denial of Decagon acquisition interest. (Yahoo Finance, October 15, source publication time not provided)[10]

## **SAIL** [Software & SaaS]
- **SailPoint** unveiled AI identity agents and runtime authorization controls at its Navigate conference; the company said Agentic Fabric and technology from its Entro acquisition were expected to be fully integrated and generally available in **November 2026**. (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[9]

## Cybersecurity Sector [Software & SaaS]
- **CRWD, PANW, FTNT, OKTA, ZS** — Shares declined **3.16%, 2.76%, 2.91%, 3.33%, and 1.50%, respectively**, on October 15 amid reported concerns about AI developers potentially competing with cybersecurity vendors; reports said OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, with no transaction announced. [report] (Yahoo Finance, published October 15; source publication time not provided)[1][2]
